intro: Correct classification does not necessarily provide a comfortable margin. Hinge loss keeps pushing examples until their signed score reaches one.
task: Return mean binary hinge loss and one documented subgradient for a linear score without regularization.
requirements: features is (n,d), labels is (n,) containing -1 or +1, weights is (d,), and bias is a scalar.
Use margin=labels*(features@weights+bias), loss=mean(maximum(0,1-margin)), and active examples with margin strictly below one.
Return {"loss": loss, "weights": -features.T@(labels*active)/n, "bias": -mean(labels*active)}. At margin exactly one, choose zero contribution.

Use real finite numeric inputs with magnitude at most 1e6, excluding booleans. Vectors have length 1..128 and matrix axes have length 1..128 unless a tighter bound is stated. Leave all inputs unchanged; raise ValueError for invalid inputs.

hints.title: Find the structure
hints.body: Build an active mask from signed margins below one; correct classifications can still belong to that mask.

hints.title: Build the calculation
hints.body: Average over every observation, including inactive ones, and assign no contribution at the exact kink.

explanation: The hinge penalty is linear when the signed score is below one and flat above one. Its active set therefore depends on the margin, not just the predicted class.
The derivative is not unique exactly at the kink. Choosing zero there gives a deterministic contract; averaging by all observations keeps the loss and gradient scales consistent.
